title: Spatiotemporal Graph Learning with Direct Volumetric Information Passing and Feature Enhancement

problem.claim: The work addresses learning spatiotemporal dynamics of physical systems across arbitrary geometric domains.

gap.claim: Existing node-edge message-passing and aggregation mechanisms limit representation learning capability.

contributions.claim: A dual-module Cell-embedded and Feature-enhanced Graph Neural Network framework, CeFeGNN, is proposed for learning spatiotemporal dynamics.
Learnable cell attributions are embedded into node-edge message passing to capture spatial dependencies of regional features and incorporate volumetric information.
A feature-enhanced block is designed to improve model performance and alleviate over-smoothing.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present CeFeGNN as a proposed dual-module framework and describe its volumetric message-passing strategy and feature-enhanced block as new design elements.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on various PDE systems and a real-world dataset are reported.
The authors report that CeFeGNN achieves superior performance compared with other baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Neural models are increasingly used for data-driven learning of physical systems, and mesh-based GNNs show potential for spatiotemporal dynamics on arbitrary geometric domains.
Standard node-edge message passing and aggregation limit representation learning capability.
CeFeGNN introduces cell embeddings into message passing, upgrading local aggregation to use volumetric and edge information, and adds feature enhancement to address over-smoothing.
Experiments across PDE systems and a real-world dataset are reported, with the authors claiming superior performance against baselines.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative performance results or metric values.
The specific PDE systems, real-world dataset, baselines, and experimental settings are unspecified.
The architecture and training procedure are not described in sufficient detail for reproduction.
The computational and memory costs of volumetric information passing are not reported.
